sonnet.problem: Card 4 already showed the answer 'Christ giving Himself up for us' on verse 2. Card 5's question repeats that fact ('Christ gave Himself up for us') and asks about the same verse, so the two cards make the same point.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card. ... Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The question says Paul gives 'another name for the immoral, impure or greedy person' and answers 'An idolater'. That applies the parenthetical '(that is, an idolater)' to all three kinds of person. In the BSB the parenthetical follows only 'greedy person', so the card settles what the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
